text: This place should not be called Mr. Wings, because when you are called something like "Mr. Wings", people would expect that wings are your specialty and they are probably really good. WRONG! This place has the absolute worst wings I have ever eaten. I didn't get to that decision by just ordering from them once. I thought that maybe it could be the guy who was cooking them, or maybe something was just wrong with my order. I went 3 times within the past 2 weeks. All the results were the same. Garbage. They offer a great variety of flavors for their wings. Mild, Medium, Hot, Nuclear, Buffalo Garlic, Golden Garlic, Honey BBQ, Smoked Honey Mustard, Caribbean Jerk, Lemon Pepper, Cajun, and Sweet Cayenne. One of the biggest problems I had with the wings were the flavors. They just didn't use enough sauce on the wings. They were dry and had barely any seasoning. I don't have pictures from all of my visits, but I did take some from my last and will share them. The most popular way people like their buffalo wings are with some sort of hot sauce with different levels of heat and flavor. I have gone all over the place to eat wings, so I have good experience with what I am eating. If the flavor is right on a wing, it can go a long way to cover for other things that might be bad. One of my favorite places to get wings offers probably the best flavoring of wings with a nice crispy outside, but the inside lacks a lot of meat. They are still my favorite because of their flavor. The "hot" wings I ordered from Mr. Wings were bland and boring (see picture). They had zero flavor. It feels almost as though they forgot to flavor them, but I saw the cook do it with my own eyes. I don't understand why it was so bad, but it was. I think they were coated in grease from the fryer, because that is all I tasted. The Caribbean Jerk wings (see picture) had a little more flavor, but was still very lacking. There was hardly anything there. Every version of wings I ever got from Mr. Wings had hardly any sauce on them. They were almost dry. It really ruined the experience for me. They did not have a lot of meat on them either. The one good thing I can say is I didn't get a lot of wings with broken bones. That always ruins the experience for me. Don't get me started on the celery that they give you. Dry, old, dirty, and some were even rubbery. What the heck! Horrible! (see picture) The blue cheese was blah. It was just creamy. No chunks of cheese. Just cream. I also ordered chicken nuggets from Mr. Wings (see picture). Did you ever go into a supermarket and buy those pre-packaged frozen wings? That is pretty much what they tasted like. They had a weak breading, were very lacking in meat, and were just too thin. McDonalds makes better nuggets! If you want buffalo wings, skip this place. They are definitely not worth the money or the time it takes to chew them.

text: Just because one avoids certain food groups doesn't mean the cravings for foods of old don't strike. Me? I had an unshakeable urge for a muffuletta, but no cheese, and definitely no meat disks. I really just wanted tangy olive salad, a creamy spread, and delicious bread. A sandwich that was great just as is- no substitutions, "let me check if we can do that", or feeling cheated by a $12 meal missing the high price items. Dude, I found it. A vegan muffuletta. It didn't come easy. First, Breads on Oak is closed Monday and Tuesday. I saw the menu and waited two long long days to make it over. Probably expressed my excitement about the sandwich three times each day. Then, when Wednesday rolled around and we rolled in, there were no more muffulettas on display! No matter, no worries, I'm not giving up so easy-and the staff was more than happy to fix me up one. Their caveat was that the ciabatta was sold out for the day, so the bread wouldn't be quite what they usually serve it with. Fine, fine, I'm starting to drool over the thought of the juicy olive salad...and the pastries right in front of me are only keeping my hunger strong. Notice the cucumber sandwich- WHAT. Been needing this in my life too. Just throw it in the bag (except don't. I'm dining in) Two sandwiches, two beautiful vegan sandwiches which do take a little bit of time to come out but there's bread samples to snack on while I wait. Two sandwiches which put the biggest smile on my face when I ate most of them in the neat, bustling bakery and then again when I munched the rest of the muffuletta while crossing the Louisiana border back to Houston. There are a few little vegan corners in New Orleans outside of the bigger restaurants, and I'm happy I found this one. They do serve cheese and seafood (not sure about meat), but everything is clearly marked. Definitely going back for a fruit tart.

text: TFS is a another company I would give a BIG Avoid. I had solar panels and a solar water heater installed by TFS. I found the quality of the Installation to be on the poor side. One of the Electrical boxes they installed is held by several washers over 1" away from the block and the installer when he was putting the clamps on the conduit broke 3 screws in the block. The installer probably had the torque on the drill too high and did not drill a pilot hole before installing the screws in the block. TFS also installed 2 rows of panels and on the 2nd row there is a space where another panel can be installed. If I was given the choice I would have opted to have another live or dummy panel installed to take up the void which is unappealing. The Solar Water Panel should also have been installed lower so it does not stick out like a sore thumb when approaching the house. The owner of TFS talked me into their Solar Water Heater system Saying that it was better than the Cornell system I already had. I gave away a Cornell System that held 80 Gallons on the roof and had a Conventional 80 Gallon water heater in the inside in case the sky was cloudy and could not heat the water. The Cornell system is a Passive system and only uses water pressure to move the water. If ther is a Powere outage one will still have Hot water. The system sold by TFS Which cost $5000 has a panel on the roof and the water is pushed up to the Panel by a pump and pulled back down by another pump. If the Electricity goes off one is in trouble especially if there is no gas and the heater works on electricity as in my case. I would never buy or have anything installed by TFS in the future.

text: Stallworth was recommended for my mother's rehabilitation twice. Once from a liver transplant and the second a fall which fractured a rib and broke her humerus. Both within weeks of one another. The first time she was admitted she had rehabilitated well for the first 4 days then slipped on a downward spiral where she was shaking immensely and emotionally unstable. PT and OT could not find out why she did so well one day, walking 150 ft to not being able to stand. About the 8th night she was transferred back to the ICU at Vanderbilt for extreme dehydration and extremely ill. After being taken out of Stallworth, she started to walk about 12 hours later. We were discharged 3 days later and because of all the reactions she had had at Stallworth, we refused to go back. We found out when she was at home she was allergic to a diuretic mediation she was being given and 3 days later my mother has a fall and ends up at Vanderbilt again and we are convinced to take her to Stallworth. We had two contingencies, one was no medication other than what Vanderbilt has given without prior consent, and two, if we ever feel uncomfortable, we would be able to leave. Both wishes were not granted. The second time she had a bad episode of depression, anxiety, and pain the first night. Second night, she is fine and tonight, her 3rd night she calls me again informing me of chest pain and muscle weakness in her legs. I believe it may be another adverse reaction to a medication. We come to find out that Stallworth was giving my mother a medicine called Seroquel, a medicine given to bipolar patients or schizophrenic patients. The nurse supervisor, José gives me a run around and later refuses to inform me if she had taken Seroquel the night before. I inform him that she is not acting herself and is complaining of chest pain, but he continues to inform me that he cannot look at the chart now because his shift has just ended. We were on the phone off and on for a hour and a half with him claiming he would call me back in twenty. Forty minutes later, no call, when I call back he says he'll call back in ten. I never received a phone call back after he informed me of the medicine Stallworth gave her. I went as far as informing him that I would have to come over and pick her up which at that he said he would not allow me to come because visitor hours ended at 8 and he would call the cops if I showed up. Stallworth is not a place to take your loved ones. They do not respect the wishes of the patients nor the caregivers. They have their own team of doctors and prescribe their own medication despite what Vanderbilt doctors have prescribed, despite caregivers wishes of not wanting any other medication given other than what the primary team has prescribed. The PT and OT are wonderful but I would be very cautious of having your loved one there due to the doctor and nursing staff. My mother went from walking with no medical problems to extreme tremors, chest pain, and mood/behaviour changes while at Stallworth. As I write this review, my mother is at the Emergency room for the second time after being at Stallworth and given the medication she was not supposed to be taking. From research, many nursing homes prescribe Seroquel when they are short staffed to help patients sleep, but Seroquel can lead to very serious side effects sometimes leading to death especially in elderly patients. PLEASE BE SURE TO CHECK ALL THE MEDS ANYONE IS PRESCRIBING for your loved ones. A

text: Service moved at a glacial pace at this place. Sorry, I really wanted to like it and the staff seemed very polite and nice and hardworking. Man, I don't get to have grits very often but these were so creamy and good. They also didn't taste overly buttery or have too much flavor but I couldn't stop eating it. Definitely my favorite part of the whole meal. The calla cakes were interesting. Never had rice balls like this and I liked it. They're also covered in powdered sugar, which also makes it tastier. text: Great meal with the August ISC crowd. Always fun to see everyone and even better when the food is fantastic. Wife and I each had an entree and we ordered an app to share with the table. No cocktails for some reason so we were out the door for about fifty bucks. Not bad given the atmosphere, the service and (above all) the food. Appetizers - I ordered the calamari but had a sample of everything that drifted by my end of the table. Thoughts: T-ravs...among the best I've had in STL and very clearly made in-house. A bit more savory than most places and served with a perfectly-executed meat sauce that someone resisted making too sweet like some other places. Best app on the table. Calamari...a close second. I really like it when a place serves the rings and the tentacles both. Pickle chips...the spicy sauce wasn't terribly spicy but it was a nice diversion from plain ranch. Pita and tzatzki...good but not my favorite app by a long shot. It would have worked better as an accompaniment for a platter of gyros or something similar. Entrees - after eyeing several of their pizzas on other tables while on the way out, I kinda wished that was what I had ordered. Food envy...it is what it is. Thoughts: Squid ink pasta with calamari...fantastically fresh pasta! The squid ink sauce was a bit thick and sufficiently flavorful that the squid was literally lost in the sauce. I love squid and it was good in this dish just a bit hidden. Great sauce too but it dominated the dish. Dolmades...Surprisingly mild flavors given the inclusion of ground lamb in the stuffing. Possibly the largest version of this dish I've ever been served but I liked the reduced ratio of grape leaf to stuffing. Also, it would have been a perfect place for the tzatzki and pita to have made an appearance but instead it was served with a choice of sides. We selected the pasta and sauce but didn't eat a bite until the next day. Wife reports it was good but I didn't get any. I don't think a single member of our group made it all the way through his or her dinner so there's nothing to report on their dessert offerings but this is certainly a place I will go back to again.

text: Best family hotel in St. Louis bar none. The lobby is amazing and has a really cool multimedia show every hour in the evening. The staff is the best staff I have ever encountered at a hotel. They go way beyond to make sure everything is perfect. Hilton should just send their trainees here and let them learn from the best. They truly were spectacular, from the bellmen to the managers. They do everything they can to make it great and their attitudes are always positive, a rarity these days. While the facility is great, the staff is what makes this hotel wonderful. There are actually 2 hotel room areas. We stayed in both as we added a day to our trip and changed rooms. The larger "new" hotel appears to be 20-30 years old but is nicely appointed and is what you would expect in a typical doubletree. Not lavish but comfortable, clean, a little dated but exactly what was expected. Full disclosure: we had a run in with bed bugs in a pull out couch for the kids. The staff was immediately responsive and remedied the situation and it was obvious that they did not want that to happen any more than we did. It can happen anywhere and is not reflective of the hotel in general. The "old" hotel is the original hotel. It is scheduled to be renovated in a few weeks. The rooms were large with high ceilings and we actually preferred the old rooms to the new. They have an old school charm but were well appointed. Can't wait to see what they do with the remodel. The common areas are really cool. It is a repurposed train station and they really keep with that theme and it's cool even if you are not a train buff (which I am not). Lots of history and charm everywhere. The kids absolutely loved it and the staff were great in helping with the scavenger hunt and making the kids feel welcome. It is not the Four Seasons and don't expect that type of stay but without question the best hotel in St. Louis, and thanks to the overall experience one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in.

Halfway through the dish, I just took out the egg, and set it aside, and after that, the whole dish was just empty. No other taste at all, so it was basically just an egg and tasteless chilli. Would've really preferred it if they would actually have some kind of flavor to the dish. Or if they actually filled it with maybe cheese or veggies. They could break up tortilla chips and cheese into the dish, and it would be better than this egg based one. I wouldn't recommend this at all, just a waste of money. You are better off making eggs at home and eating with bread. The veggie burrito was a step up from the relleno, but so is biting your nails. The burrito also lacked flavor, just didn't taste like much at all. The burrito is definitely big, so there's plenty of it, but just seemed very plain to me. I covered it with hot sauce at home, but that besides the point, because besides the heat from the sauce, this was a forgettable meal. Obviously, it's from limited choices that I picked from, and I don't know how their meat options are, but I wouldn't really recommend this place to anyone. I think I've had better food at fast food Mexican places than here. On the bright side, there is a frozen yogurt place two doors down, so you can drown out the bland taste afterwards with some frozen yogurt.

text: Simply sublime! Like a falcon, I have been stalking Peace Water like prey for months. I have driven by it so many times thinking "doesn't that place look simply scrumptious." My plans to visit never seemed to work out, until today. I might be a beer girl but I can dabble in the wine sipping on an occasion. These wines are impressive! Their winemaker is based in California and they use grapes sourced from Sonoma & Napa. For $10 you can sample up to 5 wines or you can purchase wine by the glass. I typically like my wine red & dry, I found a good variety of those options here. My favorites were the Zen (2012 Red Zinfandel), Passion (2012 Cabernet Sauvignon), and the Sublime (2012 Pinor Noir). Just listen to the sounds of the Zen...."Harmonious and tranquil, with hints of raspberry, black pepper, and baked pie." Hear that, baked pie! Buddha in a bottle indeed! Other things that impressed me: (Y) - Family is a stong central focus here. Their son Jordan, who was also our wine sommelier (great guy by the way....very genuine, attentive, and helpful) designed the space. He has a degree in architecture. Laura, his mother did the decorating. It has a cozy indie arts & vintage marketplace feel. You can't help but stare at the lighting details and that fancy crystal chandelier over the bar. Little lights are draped all along the ceiling. Lots of cute seating areas. Several near the fireplace.The theme here is obvious and would make any hippie proud. Peace & love! I think I am in love with that large circular cozy nook (by the fire). I will call it "the buddha room" it's perfect for groups. It would also be great for wine & massage nights similar to "mead & knead" events held at New Day Meadery. (Y) - 50% of their profits go to 8 charities throughout the year selected by the families 8 children. Charities are displayed on the "Giving Wall." Each time you buy a bottle you are given a token. You choose which charity you wish to donate with your token. I don't know about you but I think that is pretty groovy (I am sticking with the theme here). (Y) - If you join the Peace Posse wine club, wine will personally be delivered to your home by Reggie their vintage 1966 21 window VW hippie van! This along with other perks make joining this club sound like true Nirvana. (Y) - The bar area is 21+ but families with kids are welcome in "the Buddha room". (Y) - If you have friends or family that love peace signs they will love the bottle art which includes a peace sign. The bottle corks tie back into the family theme and use a design to include the hands of their 8 children. It's all in those details! Future Plans/Notes: Front & back outdoor seating areas are part of their future master plans. Also, distribution of their wines will be coming soon to local restaurants & bars in Indy. Lots of wonderful things happening here that simply make me want to say "Give Peace a chance" you won't regret it.

text: Cool atmosphere and all that stuff, but the food has much to be desired. First our party was offered the choice between sparkling and still water. Like a virgin gin and tonic or something... During our pre-dinner water session we joke that "Oh, they are obviously going to charge us $5 for this..." and laugh it off. After we finish the water, the server asks if we wanted to start another bottle, we all look at each other, chuckle, and decline. Maybe its true? We then ordered a handful of their happy hour cocktails, these were pretty good. Fresh fruit, good composition. Good portions and a good price. I dig it. We also order a happy hour plate of nachos knowing that it will be rather small. The nachos come out and there are literally 4 tortilla chips on the plate under the heap of nacho stuff. This isn't a big complaint, but the chips are probably the cheapest part and they ended up bringing out more chips anyway. Why not just have a suitable amount of chips to begin with? Again, this isn't a huge complaint, but more of an odd observation. Now for the main course, I ordered the pork banh mi (which is misspelled as bahn on the menu) and my cohorts ordered the Big Boy Burger. Wow, those burgers looked freaking awesome. My banh mi however, had much to be desired. It was served on a soft roll with a tiny piece of pork belly which barely took up half of the roll itself. The sandwich was nothing to write home about, but it wasn't bad by any means, just lacking. I am more blown away by my snacks relative size to the comparatively priced big boy burger, which was literally the size of my head. We enjoyed our meals, my friends had another meal worth of left overs, and I am left looking for a snack at home. To top it off the water was $5 on our meal. What the hell? I've been here a hand full of times and every time I've tried so hard to like the place, but its just never anything special. The drinks are alright, the food is okay, but there are a ton of places in Tucson that have so much more to offer without the inconsistency and oddities that Paso has.

We were able to browse menus while we waited, as you stay in line as you move inside (and order at the counter) before receiving a number and being loosely directed towards available tables. Anna had a Bloody Mary and Dan had a craft beer. I needed caffeine so I had a delicious Arnold Palmer. Anna treated us to my favorite part of the meal... BONUTS. Fried biscuit dough (AMAZING) with sugar, lemon mascarpone, and blueberry compote. I seriously think that when I come back, I will make this my main meal, so I can have them all for myself. My. new. favorite. thing. I had a lot of trouble making up my mind for my main dish, because the menu at the restaurant is much more extensive than the truck's used to be. I decided that for my first visit, I needed to go with my old truck standby, the SEC: biscuit, smoked sausage, egg, and aged cheddar. I had the egg scrambled because I was in the midst of sensory overload when I ordered; I usually prefer the egg fried. But it was delicious nonetheless! Even better than the truck days, honestly... although I wonder if it's because I was eating it in air conditioning at a table with real silverware vs. plastic fork at the market. I also ordered sides of the "chronic" bacon which was sticky and sweet, and the potatoes. The potatoes I wish were a bit crispier, but the bacon was fab. Bacon purists might prefer the normal bacon, but I love a little sweetness with the salt. You guys, do yourself a favor and hit up Biscuit Love... I'm so glad I could take my friend Anna (and Dan, too!) to brunch there, and to meet Karl. I'm so happy for the Worleys and this new adventure, and hoping they put another location in Franklin someday!

text: Many years ago, before the age of television and cars, people were entertained by going to huge movie houses located conveniently close to major public transportation stops. One of these palaces was located at Suburban Square, it was the "Suburban" movie theater and what was cool about it was that it had a semi-circular lobby and two entrances - one on Coulter and one on St. James Place. Alas, that age is gone, and one of the early casualties was the Suburban. It closed in 1979. It was subsequently a farmer's market, which at first was 'bare bones' and then became more 'upscale'. Then it became a clothing store. Now it is the site of a Not Your Average Joe's location. NYAJ has actually made use of the curving marquee, converting it to a dining patio above street level. Why am I telling you all this? Because the thing I liked most was that the restaurant pays homage of a sort to the history of the building. One two story wall has the word "SUBURBAN" in silver letters near the top and a smooth space where they project movie trailers - everything from "Lawrence of Arabia" to "Ferris Bueller's Day Off". This was not something I'd expect a chain to do, and it pleased me. The Reverend Dr. Steak and I had an enjoyable lunch there. Unusually, we both chose the meatloaf. Usually we make an effort to get different items, both so we can sample more of the menu and so we can get a better sense of the offerings for ourselves. Alas, the spaghetti squash bolognese was not available for lunch that day, and that meatloaf looked so darn good. It generally did not disappoint, served almost as a sandwich with mashed potato "Bun" and fried onion strings. The sauce - BBQ - was quite tasty. The dish relies on these elements, as the meat itself is fairly tasteless. Be warned: Don't order it plain. That would disappoint. Service was excellent, attentive, thoughtful and friendly. Price was reasonable. We'll be back, and next time we'll do our best to broaden our choices.

As the night was coming to a close we headed back to the Santa Photo station to pick up our pre-paid photos with Santa, only to find that the photographers and all of the 'helpers' had left for the evening, even though the event was still open for 15 more minutes. We found a member of security to ask "Do you know where we can find our photos?" (hoping that they would be left for us at the front gate, or something equally as convenient.) text: I have literally never dealt with a physician that is so childish, unprofessional, and incompetent as Tracy Young. Our daughter went to urgent care after rolling her ankle at XC. We have a lot of experience with this ankle - a previous grade 3 sprain from basketball. We're well-educated and used to working with respectable doctors/urgent care/hospital staff out-of-state for sprains, dislocated knees, orthopedics, etc., i.e., we know what a good doctor sounds like and looks like. Tracy Young is not quality care. Even our 14-year-old daughter noticed. Young didn't compare her ankle to her healthy ankle, didn't test her ligaments / mobility... all she did was poke the ankle, "does this hurt?" "does this hurt?" X-rays were taken to confirm nothing broken. Based on the poking of the ankle, the diagnosis was a Grade 1 or 2 level sprain. The verbal instructions were the usual - RICE and wear a cast (though Young gave no instruction on how long to wear it - we knew from past experience to wear it for the week or two it was healing so that the ligaments can heal w/o risk of re-injuring). We were instructed to go to an orthopedic specialist if pain got worse - again, typical. She verbally tells both our daughter and her father to stay off of it for 1-2 weeks while it healed. Standard. Our daughter could barely walk on her ankle so she stayed home the next day. By end of weekend, she was able to walk better, but touching it or stretching still causes pain. Sprains take awhile to heal as we all know. So, Monday comes around and the note Young provided at end of visit didn't excuse our daughter from PE. Standard practice would be for the doctor to write a note excusing physical activity like RUNNING while healing. Sasha's dad didn't ask; doctor / nurse didn't ask. The school calls and wants this note. I speak to Tricia and say I need note excusing daughter from PE for the 1-2 week period doctor said stay off of it. Tricia seemed nice enough; said she'd call me back if there were any problems. Why would there be a problem you might ask? Because Tracy Young apparently doesn't like details or specifics or putting anything in writing. Tricia calls back and says we need to go to orthopedic if we want a note. What!?!?!? So, I argue we need THIS doctor that diagnosed her and that we paid $100 (plus what our insurance pays!) to write a damn note! She doesn't need an ortho... she needs to rest it per YOUNG for 1-2 weeks while she heals. Tricia apparently doesn't know how to handle "no... you all need to do the job that we paid for" because she said I'd need to talk to the doctor... FOR A NOTE to excuse an injured kid THEY diagnosed! Young gets on the phone herself ... Oh. My. Word. I have never experienced such an unprofessional "physician" in all my life. I was talking to my husband when she got on the phone and she starts screaming in my ear, "HELLO! HELLO! HELLO! HELLO! HELLO!" Jesus lady - that certainly sets the tone. I had to get my husband to listen in - it was so incredible! Her childish tone, her misinformation, her talking over me, her ARGUING about writing a note based on HER diagnosis... It was honestly pretty funny if it weren't for the fact I needed a note from her! She kept saying I didn't say what I needed - PERHAPS if you didn't keep talking over me! - and she didn't understand the request... How long have you been practicing that you don't understand the concept of a note for school based on an injury?!?! Do you not treat children and know schools will ask for this? She agreed our daughter shouldn't be on it, resting for several weeks, so why the argument? Why couldn't Tricia just do it? Because this lady has serious control/anger issues. If you want a thorough exam, specific documentation (we had to ask her to write down the level of sprain, too, while in office, because we know healing is very different between the grades!), a trustworthy, professional doctor - AVOID this place ... NEVER experienced anything like it; FOR A NOTE!!! Young was so unprofessional we are considering filing a complaint with our insurance company!

text: Apparently my 30's have brought on a bout of butterfingers. The first time I needed to get it fixed/replaced, I did a ton of research to find the right place. Cost wasn't a factor, since the crack was so bad that my screen blacked out, so I just wanted it fixed as fast as possible. Most places told me it would take 24 hours, or at least a few. When I called Celltek, I was told it would only take 20 minutes! I hung up my friend's phone and drove right over. The second time was just as speeding. And even though I figured my phone was just getting old, I asked if he knew why it was having issues connecting to the charger. He got some tweezer type of tool out and dug out a bunch of fuzzy matter(he said it was just pocket lint) from the charging input and now it works better than ever. Didn't even charge me for the extra help. The third time took almost two hours, since he was in the middle of several other projects when I came in. I didn't mind at all because of the great customer service. Also on my last visit I had him instal a new home button since mine had become rarely responsive with age. Only charged $20. Yay. More good news-They charge at least $10 less for screen replacement than the other places I checked out. Super friendly, super knowledgeable, super efficient and super affordable. Btw... One reviewer complained about paying $6 for the parking lot that Celltek is near. Easy fix- Just park in the Marshalls garage across the street! It's free for the first 75min.

text: Husk features nouveau southern food that is markedly uneven. The menu claims daily rotation, but doesn't seem to change much day to day. Among the entrees at our table the Plate of Southern Vegetables was by far the standout and one of the best vegetarian dishes in the city. A lamb entree was flavorful and well cooked, but tiny in size. The beef, catfish, and swordfish entrees were all ok, but neither inventively prepared nor paired with great vegetables or grains. Chocolate and coconut pies were solid, but unspectacular. Given the price point and decidedly inexpensive proteins ($28 for catfish?!) I expected a lot more of a wow factor. Husk seems to aim more for well prepared Southern staples, rather than high brow interpretations. And if you're looking for Southern staples, Nashville is rife with them at lower prices points and better service. The hipster server vibe at Husk (replete with flannel shirts and handlebar mustaches) continued over to cooly inattentive service. The menu was never explained in detail and questions were met with curt replies. Alcohol orders were forgotten and our whole table sat with empty water glasses. Overall an interesting concept that likely won't last once the novelty has worn off. There are too many new restaurants in Nashville serving the exact same type of cuisine with better food and service.

text: Let's get right to the point. If I could eat here every day, I would. My personal go to is to get the empanadas to start. Oh, those empanadas! At only $1 a piece, I could gorge myself on probably 5 (or 10!) and be completely satisfied. Unlike what people typically associate with empanadas, I believe these use corn flour which leads to... I guess you can say an almost cornbread texture versus the typical flour that produces a more doughy wrap. The meat on the inside is delicious and if you add some picante salsa... Mmm! Just thinking about it makes me hungry again. But it doesn't stop there! Then I order the Bandeja Montañera. At $16.50 a pop, it may seem pretty pricey but once they bring out the veritable mountain of food, you'll realize it's well worth it. This plate is comprised of either carne a la parilla or carne molida (grilled steak or ground beef, I always get the carne a la parilla), salchichas (sausage), chicharron (pork skin) for the main meats then rice, red beans, platanos, egg, corn cake, and salad as the sides. The carne a la parilla is very savory and packs a lot of flavor for being such a thin slice of meat. The way the salchichas is spiced is... I would say almost on the sweet side and oh so delicious. And the chicharron? Oh. When that is prepared correctly, the skin is so crispy that even as you take bites knowing that it's not at all healthy for you, you just don't care. And still, it goes on! Even though you know you'll be taking at least half of your entree home, you can't help but eye the goodies displayed in the bakery cases. I always get the flan ($2.50). It's light but still has a decent density to it that it doesn't just feel like jello in your mouth and is sweet enough to hit the spot but not overbearingly so. Even when I feel like I can't eat anymore, I'd still want another slice of it! Pair that with a cafe con leche ($2.00) to fight the food coma you've undoubtedly induced on yourself and I'd say it's the perfect end to a fantastic meal. In short, La Pequeña Colombia serves up plates of deliciousness from start to finish that I don't know how anyone could ever leave there unhappy. Side tip: This place can get crowded, and rightfully so, so prepare for that by either heading out early for lunch or dinner.

text: AWFUL AWFUL AWFUL! This business has evolved into a nightmare. Zero stars is more fitting to describe this terrible business. I was a loyal customer of this veterinary practice for 18 years before the VCA corporate entity took over. I can't remember when the practice changed their name to VCA Neshaminy Hospital but since then, they've turned into a "sell sell sell everything you can" kind of business. Even though I noticed some of the staff had tried this approach with me, I still felt comfortable with taking my cats there, so long as the doctor who was our "regular" vet saw to them. She has always been trustworthy for the 18 years I had taken my cats to see her and she truly CARES for the pets she treats. Imagine that-- a vet who simply examines, diagnoses and makes appropriate recommendations for the sake of helping pets without using them as a selling platform. It was only after I saw a different vet (because my "regular" vet wasn't working that night) did the nightmare begin. My 12 week old Himalayan Seal Point kitten was neutered and vaccinated at VCA. My regular vet oversaw all of this and, as usual, she did a great job. Everything was fine until he reached the age of 10 months. I took him to VCA on a weeknight after noticing that something was growing increasingly wrong with his left eye. Our "regular" vet was not working that night. Had she been on-schedule, maybe my kitten would have been spared what he'd experience later on because of one very unprofessional veterinarian. I made an appointment to see VCA's new "medical director" Dr. Thorndyke, who diagnosed my kitten with pink eye. Yet, she pointed out a large ulcer on his eye during that same visit. In hindsight, I realize pinkeye had nothing to do with that ulcer. But I didn't have a chance to log on to the internet and research feline eye conditions at that very moment. I trusted and believed her. Isn't that how it's supposed to work when you take your pet to see a vet? You trust them to make a proper diagnosis and prescribe appropriate treatment? I thought that's how it worked since my regular vet had always done right by my pets. Dr. Thorndyke prescribed an eye ointment and said we should return 7 days later for a progress check. The total cost of this visit was about $200, yet she barely spent 10 minutes with us in the exam room. Her tone with me was short, condescending and dismissive. After the next 7 days of administering this ointment, my kitten's condition worsened. I returned to VCA and a different vet was professional enough to admit that my kitten's condition required a specialist. Again, my "regular" vet wasn't working that day. I later learned that her hours were immensely scaled back at this veterinary-turned-sales office.But that's beside the point of my review. The second vet referred my kitten to VSEC in Levittown, PA. If anyone has taken their pet to VSEC in Levittown, they know it's not easy to get a 'same day' appointment with a specialist unless it's a true emergency. The 2nd VCA vet who examined my kitten personally called VSEC to relay the urgency of the situation and my kitten was seen to, on that same day, 2 hours later. One eye surgery, many visits and approximately $3,500 dollars later, my kitten is healing. VSEC's ophthalmologist diagnosed a (very painful) corneal ulcer and operated on my kitten. Since the ulcer had time to burrow deeper into his eye because of the time that passed in-between our awful visit to Dr. Thorndyke and his operation, I only hope my kitten will regain full sight in his left eye, as he continues to heal from this experience. Only after learning more about VSEC's diagnosis and comparing it to pink eye, did I learn how negligent and harmful Dr. Thorndyke's diagnosis was to my kitten. I feel very sorry for anyone who would trust their pet to VCA Neshaminy Hospital and will never return there again. Wow, look at the review from a Californian customer who was full of compliments for both vets who examined my kitten before one of them referred us to VSEC. I'm delighted to know Dr. Thorndyke has improved on her professional responsibilities since her abysmal "treatment" of my kitten. I never saw the Californian customer's review prior to posting mine. But, once again, I suppose that's beside the point. The main point is this: VCA Neshaminy Hospital is absolutely AWFUL.

I also have a consistently pleasant experience with the service at Han Dynasty. The food comes out very quickly and the waiters are generous with water and tea refills. For Han first-timers, here are some of my favorite dishes that I recommend: - spicy crispy cucumbers - cumin beef (very spicy!) - garlic style chicken (milder but very tasty) - double cooked fish (the waiter told us it's the staff's favorite! very delicious) - dan dan noodles, of course

text: I have been able to take a few trips on a variety of occasions with Bada Bing Limo, and it will certainly be the only place I ever consider when the need arises to transport a bunch of people anywhere. The entirety of my experience with them has been in their big 14 person party bus, and I am convinced there is not a more fun way to get around. The owner of the business was our driver on all occasions, and he has a fantastic mix of being a professional while also setting a really fun mood and having a good time with the people riding with him. The party bus itself is awesome. I've been on it at full capacity as well as with a few extra seats open. If I was doing a long trip somewhere, it makes sense to maybe leave one or two people at home, but in a trip across town there is plenty of room to take advantage of their max capacity. The inside is much nicer than some of the other buses I have been on. The floors weren't sticky, there wasn't a smell of stale booze in the air, and the black leather seats, wood counters, and decorative mirrors are much classier than some other offerings of the same service. The windows have blinds that you can shut if it gets too bright outside, and there is even a big TV that picks up satellite signal so you can have that on during your trip. The bus is outfitted with plenty of trash receptacles built into the bus so you don't have open bags of trash in the middle of your group. It has different built in ice chests that were filled with ice to keep drinks cold in, and lots of cup holders so you can set drinks down (although I don't know why you would want to do that). The sound system gets plenty loud, and can be connected via Bluetooth so you don't even need to plug your phone into the system to play and control the music. There was plenty of room for our beverages in the built in coolers and space on the floor or counters to put other things we brought onboard, but I think he also had room in the back to store anything that you didn't want in the main cabin, which seems like something that would be especially beneficial if you were going to a tailgate. Be sure to ask about trips like winery tours or even a venture from Indy down to some stops on the bourbon trail and back, too. Last but certainly not least, they obviously have a strong focus on making sure that they deliver a safe ride, and I never felt like there was anything to worry about from the time we got on and were instructed about the safety procedures to the time we got off at the end of the day.

text: Despite the low number of stars and bad reviews we wanted to try Tace for ourselves and give it a good chance because New Orleans fare is one of our favorites. We thought when we walked in, 'hey the place is packed' so it has to be good, right?...nope. It pains me to have to give a new restaurant a 1 star, but I have to. Tace is a huge disappointment. From beginning to end there are issues. Although the hostess was pleasant, she had no idea that a party that had reserved for 7:30 was already eating in the restaurant. Mind you, we arrived at around 8:30, so the reservation shouldn't have mattered. Not a big deal. We and a party of 4 behind us was able to be seated. It took a while for the server to come to take our orders, but we knew what we wanted. The server came over and counted tables to figure out what number table we were. Again, not a big deal, but I noticed. I ordered the Barbecue Shrimp...my favorite New Orleans dish. I asked if the Barbecued Shrimp was like Brennan's or Pascales and the server had no idea what I was talking about and then told me that it was only her 5th day. So, I asked how many shrimp was in the order, she said about 5 and that they are the big prawns (which in NOLA you always get big prawns with barbecued shrimp). I decided not to ask anymore questions. I also ordered Fried Green Tomatoes. We tried ordering red beans and rice, but they were out. What?! How can a New Orleans style restaurant run out of red beans and rice? A bad feeling was coming on. As we waited I looked around and noticed many tables getting wrong orders and servers calling out wrong names of plates, then making excuses for not knowing what the items were. What looked to be a band came in and started setting up, however after a while we noticed that pop music was playing...not Jazz. I then realized that the Hispanic "band members" were there for something that was going on later because I noticed the bar area started to be patronized by Hispanic women in party-style dresses (salsa night maybe?). We saw a picture of the bread from someones visit a month earlier on Yelp, so we were eager to try it. We were instead brought the bottoms of dinner rolls with butter. It definitely wasn't the same bread. The water I asked for with lots of lemon had the end of a lemon sliced thin and thrown in the water...pet peeve to have the lemon in the water and not on the side or side of cup. Most of the lemon wasn't squeezable becasue it was just the peel sliced. So, I see a server from another table bring what appeared to be our food to a table across the room. I watched as they called out the food and placed plates down...I saw my Fried Green Tomatoes...and not to be the judgmental bastard or anything, but those people didn't look like the type to order Fried Green Tomatoes. I then saw the waiter look at the ticket and mouth, "oh these items belong to another table" and he looked over and saw me staring at him. So he went to the back with the plate and another server came out and gave me the same plate. The rest of our disappointing looking meals came out and our server called out, Shrimp and Grits. I said, "No one at our table ordered Shrimp and Grits. I ordered Barbecued Shrimp." "Oh, that's what I meant," said the server and as she put down the plate in front of me. I gasped. "Uh why is there rice in my plate!" She said , "That's how we serve it." Not only was rice in the plate, but there were big hunks of onion and an extremely dark barbecue sauce in the bowl. The shrimp were medium sized shrimp, not large prawns and they were shelled and butterflied. Well all but one was butterflied. The shrimp also had the veins still in them. Why wouldn't you de-vein the shrimp if you went through the trouble to butterfly these little shrimps? The look and taste of this dish was all wrong. It didn't taste like Brennan's or Pascals. It was just wrong. Barbecued Shrimp from NOLA isn't really barbecued at all. They are big prawns drowned in a butter based sauce and made with Abeita beer or some sort of liquor. The sauce at Tace was trying to be barbecue sauce out of a bottle. Nothing tasted great and a lot of it tasted bad. Bad would definitely be my Barbecued Shrimp, my husband's Seafood Beignets and the booty bread. The okays: my Fried Green Tomatoes, my daughter's Caesar Salad (although too much mayo) and my son's Seafood Gumbo (couldn't' see the seafood and that was the most shallow bowl I've ever encountered...the gumbo was only really painted onto the plate as my son could barely fill his spoon with the gumbo). This place will not make it if they don't make a change. My suggestions: 1. Go to NOLA and eat your heart out, then find a Chef that can actually cook NOLA style food. 2. Train your servers. Let the servers eat every dish. Give your servers a lesson in NOLA food and history. Train your servers on the layout of your restaurant, expediting food, and serving the food to the correct tables and seats.

text: I adopted a kitten with a Neurological disorder in March 2015. I brought the kitty home, he got along great with our two cats and was living a very happy and healthy lifestyle or so I thought. To make a long story short, in early October our baby starting having cluster seizures, so badly that not even anti-seizure medication would work. We ended up having to put him down and are still heartbroken. While I was fully aware I was adopting a Special Needs cat, I was led to believe that his condition was mild and would not affect his quality of life. Tell that to the 10 month old cat I put down...I am upset because I lost one of my fur babies and because I feel I was so grossly misled to the severity of his condition. If you do not understand the severity of a condition, you have no right placing that cat for adoption. It just leads to broken hearts and empty homes...I urge the SPCA to have a VET talk to potential adopting families so they can get proper information from a DOCTOR before adoption...avoid the heartbreak.

text: I was given a McDonald's Gift Card, with a note telling me not every meal out needs to be a "Yelp" night out. My cousin told me, "You need to slum it once in a while". I carried it in my wallet for almost a year, before I finally used it. Many times I thought of giving it to a homeless person begging at a stoplight, but I'd always give them a dollar instead. The other day, I skipped breakfast and as lunch approached I was starving. I was pressed for time and wanted something quick. I just passed a billboard promoting McDonald's new Triple Cheeseburger and thought of my gift card. I pulled in to the first McDonald's I saw and placed my order. It was a simple order, a Triple Cheeseburger and Coke. My Coke was cold and refreshing. I enjoy an occasional fountain soda. Especially if the soda lines are kept clean, like these were. The soda taste so much better. My Triple Cheeseburger on the other hand was disappointing. It had me wondering if I really was eating beef. Yes, it was fresh and hot but lacked any flavor. It was on special for $2 and I still feel as if I overpaid. Staff is friendly and fast, as it should be at a fast food joint.

text: Tried this place for lunch, after reading some of the good reviews here, but I was not impressed...AT ALL. So, I will likely not be returning. The adana kebab platter has just two strips. Total rip off for the price. The meat too chewy, it should've been cooked longer. The sandwiches are in very soggy pita wraps, too much lettuce and pickle in them. They're more like tacos with pickle in them. They're served with regular thick cut french fries. That's not authentic Mediterranean/middle eastern food. That's like eating fries with a burger at Five Guys. The food was bland...let me say very bland. I have eaten authentic middle eastern and mediterranean food, so the taste and flavors are not new to me. I think they need to sample some of the other middle-eastern restaurants to improve their menu and taste, even other similar restaurants in NYC or Canada. What's good -- polite male server/host. Plenty of parking, convenient location right off rt 73. Ambiance is ok, but I don't go to a restaurant for it's decor, so that doesn't matter, as long as it looks clean, which this did. It's more like a fake middle-eastern ambiance, with tacky desert palm trees on the front windows, etc. to create the theme...again, the decor doesn't matter to me.
label: NEG
